items.stem: Explain why friction is not always equal to μR.
items.answer: μR is the maximum (limiting) value; friction only takes the value needed to prevent motion, up to μR. When sliding or on the point of sliding, F = μR.
items.markingKey: B1 F ≤ μR; B1 equality only when limiting or moving [2]

items.stem: Explain why the coefficient of friction μ between a block and the ground has no units, and state what a larger value of μ means.
items.answer: μ = F/R is a ratio of two forces, so it has no units; a larger μ means a rougher contact that can provide more friction for the same normal reaction.
items.markingKey: B1 ratio of forces; B1 rougher contact [2]

items.stem: A block of mass 4 kg rests on rough horizontal ground (μ = 0.333) and is pulled by a force of 8 N at 40° above the horizontal. It does not move. Mohammed says the friction force is μR = 11.6 N. Explain the error.

items.stem: Explain why the force needed to push a block up a rough slope at constant speed is greater than the force needed to stop it sliding down.
items.answer: Pushing up, friction acts down the slope with the weight component, so P = mg sin α + μR; holding it, friction helps, acting up the slope, so P = mg sin α − μR.
items.markingKey: B1 friction direction reverses; B1 the two expressions [2]

items.markingKey: B1 friction up the slope; B1 correct acceleration [2]

items.answer: (a) 3.14 m s⁻¹ (b) include air resistance, which would reduce the speed further

items.stem: A block of mass 2 kg on rough horizontal ground is pulled by a force of 15 N at 25° above the horizontal. Mei takes the normal reaction as 20 N. Explain the error.
items.answer: The pull has an upward component 15 sin 25°, so R = 20 − 6.34 = 13.7 N.

items.stem: A block of mass 10 kg on rough horizontal ground is pulled by a force of 10 N at 15° above the horizontal. Elena takes the normal reaction as 100 N. Explain the error.

items.stem: Show that whether a block placed at rest on a rough slope inclined at 25° slides does not depend on its mass, and decide whether it slides when μ = 0.5.
items.answer: It slides if mg sin α > μmg cos α, i.e. tan α > μ: m cancels. tan 25° = 0.466, so it does not slide.

items.stem: A block slides down a rough plane inclined at 30° with μ = 0.25. Kwame finds its acceleration as g(sin α + μ cos α) = 7.17 m s⁻². Explain the error.
items.answer: Friction opposes the motion, so it acts up the slope: a = g(sin α − μ cos α) = 2.83 m s⁻².
items.markingKey: B1 friction up the slope; B1 correct acceleration [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) What does modelling a string as inextensible mean? (b) What does modelling a string as light mean?
items.answer: (a) it does not stretch, so connected particles have the same speed and acceleration (b) its mass is negligible, so the tension is the same throughout
items.markingKey: (a) Inextensible means fixed length. (b) A light string has no weight.

items.stem: A block slides down a plane inclined at 45°. Noah models the plane as smooth and predicts an acceleration of 7.07 m s⁻²; the measured acceleration is 5.66 m s⁻². Explain the difference and state how the model should be refined.
items.answer: The real plane is rough; friction opposes the motion. Modelling it as rough with μ = 0.2 gives a = g(sin α − μ cos α) = 5.66 m s⁻².
items.markingKey: B1 friction ignored in the smooth model; B1 refined model with friction [2]
